obs_text: In 2Pet.1.8, ἀργός/ἄκαρπος (M67) modifies the state of the believer's relation to M15 (knowledge/ἐπίγνωσις) -- the diligence-cluster term functions as the negative condition that increasing virtues (qualities named in v.5-7) are said to prevent, making M67 the hinge describing failure-mode outcome relative to M15's positive content.

In Rom.12.11, σπουδή/ζέω (M67 zeal + M69 fervent) stand together with M47 (spirit/πνεῦμα) and M78 (serve/δουλεύω), with ὀκνηρός (M67, slothful) as the negative to be avoided -- M67's own vantage adds that this is a triad of intensifiers (not lagging, being fervent, serving the Lord) where zeal is the connective quality binding inward fervor of spirit to outward service.

The verse's operation word is παρακαλέω ('pleaded', T3-tagged in role list), initiated by the elders (subject, implicit party) and directed toward Jesus (accusative object, party present, T7/T8-tagged) on behalf of the centurion. σπουδαίως (M67, T2) intensifies the manner of this operation but is not itself the T3-tagged operation word.

No other M-code characteristic is present in Luke.7.4's role list; σπουδαίως (M67) stands alone here, intensifying the pleading (παρακαλέω) directed at Jesus concerning the centurion's worthiness (ἄξιος, itself not M-tagged in this list).

In Rom.12.11, ὀκνηρός (M67) stands paired with σπουδή/M67's own zeal-term and alongside M69 (fervent/ζέω), M47 (spirit/πνεῦμα), and M78 (serve/δουλεύω) -- M67's own vantage adds that the negated disposition (not being slothful) is the necessary precondition cleared before the positive triad of zeal, fervor of spirit, and service to the Lord can be enacted; the verse structures M67 as both negative prohibition and positive command in a single breath.

The operation word 'write' (G1125, role-T3) is the object of the eagerness (G4710); the author (a party, 'I') initiates the intended act of writing directed toward 'you' (the recipients, a party) concerning their common salvation.

No prior context recorded. From eagerness's own vantage: this verse pairs the author's eagerness with M79 (salvation) as its intended topic and M44 (contend) and M13 (faith) as the redirected actual purpose - eagerness here functions as the initial impulse that is redirected into the necessity of defending the faith, showing a contrast between intended and actual epistolary purpose.

The operation word 'know' (G1492I, role-T3) is directed by the master (a party, 'his master') toward the servant (a party, 'you wicked and slothful servant') as a rhetorical accusation: the master initiates the charge of knowing (or failing to act on known expectations) against the servant characterized as slothful.

No prior context recorded. From sloth's own vantage: this verse pairs slothfulness with M58 (wicked, ponēros) as twin epithets applied by the master to the servant (M78) - sloth here functions as the specific charge of inactivity that, alongside wickedness, together constitute the master's condemnation; sloth is thus one half of a dual accusation rather than standing alone.

The operation word 'write' (G1125, role-T3) is present and directed by Paul (a party, 'my') toward 'you' (the Philippians, a party), but the 'trouble' term (G3636) itself functions as a predicate describing writing's quality, not as the initiator or recipient of a separate operation.

No prior context recorded. From this characteristic's vantage: 'trouble' (G3636) here is paired with M19 (safe, asphales) as a positive complement - repeating instruction is framed as no burden (G3636) and as a safeguard (M19) for the readers, showing the two characteristics work together to justify Paul's repetition as beneficial rather than burdensome.

Eccl.10.18 also carries M24 (H6103, sloth) and M23/M72 (H3027G, hand). From indolence's own vantage: H8220 supplies the causal/resultative link -- it names the condition (slack-handed idleness) that translates the disposition of sloth (M24) into the physical outcome via the hand (M23/M72), i.e. indolence is the mechanism connecting sloth-as-disposition to hand-as-instrument, producing the house's collapse. No prior cluster context exists for this verse.

Matt.20.3 has role-T3 operation words G1831 (going out), G2476 (standing). G0692 (idle) is an adjective describing the state of 'others' (the party) found standing in the marketplace -- it does not itself initiate an operation but characterizes the party's condition as the object of the householder's seeing/going-out action, directed toward them.

Matt.20.3 also carries M15 (G1492H, saw) alongside G0692. From idleness's own vantage: the idleness of 'others' is precisely the state that the M15 seeing-action discovers/targets -- G0692 supplies the object-condition that motivates the householder's seeing and subsequent action (hiring), i.e. idleness is what is perceived. No prior cluster context exists for this verse.

In Isa.12.1, thanksgiving (H3034) is directly bound to M02 (anger, H0599/H0639G) and M11/M81 (turning away, H7725I) and M11/M45 (comfort, H5162G): the thanksgiving is explicitly the response TO God's anger having turned and to his comforting action -- thanksgiving here functions as the verbal capstone/response completing the arc from divine anger through reversal to comfort. No prior context exists for this verse; this is the first pass.

In 2Chr.7.3, thanksgiving (H3034) is paired with M22 (glory, H3519) and M07/M50 (steadfast love, H2617A) and M05/M18 (good, H2896A): the people's giving of thanks is triggered by witnessing God's glory descending, and the content of the thanks-refrain names God's goodness and enduring steadfast love -- thanksgiving here is the responsive verbal act that names and ratifies the other characteristics (glory, goodness, covenant love) just witnessed. No prior context exists for this verse; this is the first pass.

In Rom.1.8, thanksgiving (G2168) is directly grounded in and directed toward the recipients' M13 (faith, G4102G) which is 'proclaimed in all the world' -- the apostle's thanksgiving is a response to another's faith-characteristic being manifest. No prior context exists for this verse; this is the first pass.

In Rom.7.25, thanksgiving (G2168) is the response that resolves the conflict named by M78 (serve/enslavement, G1398), M54 (law, G3551, x2), M15 (mind, G3563), M47 (flesh, G4561), and M56 (sin, G0266): thanksgiving is offered precisely because of deliverance from this tangle of enslaving characteristics, functioning as the verbal pivot from struggle to gratitude. No prior context exists for this verse; this is the first pass.

In 1Cor.1.4, thanksgiving (G2168) is explicitly grounded in M50 (grace, G5485) 'given to you in Christ Jesus' -- thanksgiving here functions as the recognized, verbalized response to grace received, making grace the material cause of the thanksgiving. No prior context exists for this verse; this is the first pass.
No other M-code characteristic co-occurs alongside thanksgiving (G2168) in Eph.5.20's role list.

In Col.1.3, M42 (prayer, G4336) is also present, but functions as the paired but distinct practice ('we thank God ... when we pray for you') -- thanksgiving and prayer are companion but not merged acts; no deeper structural dependency is shown here beyond co-occurrence in the same devotional act.

In Col.3.15, the adjective 'thankful' (G2170) is commanded in the immediate context of M33 (peace, G1515) ruling in the heart and M47 (heart, G2588) as the site where that peace and thankfulness reside -- thankfulness here is the disposition that accompanies and issues from Christ's peace governing the heart, presented as a fitting response to the unity of the one body. No prior context exists for this verse; this is the first pass.

This is the first pass over this verse. H3034 (praise) co-occurs with M01 (awesome, H3372H) and M13/M61 (Holy, H6918G): praise here is the human response summoned by the fearsome and holy character of God's name — the thanksgiving-praise cluster functions as the vocal/liturgical outworking triggered by the awe/holiness characteristics present.

First pass over this verse. H3034 (confession, Hithpael) co-occurs with M42 (prayed, H6419), M74 (keeps/keep, H8104G), M44 (covenant, H1285), M07/M50 (steadfast love, H2617A), M51 (love, H0157G), M01 (awesome, H3372H), and M54 (commandments, H4687): confession here functions within the prayer-act as acknowledgment of God's covenant faithfulness, situating thanksgiving/confession as the human response that opens into intercessory prayer grounded in God's covenant-keeping love.

First pass over this verse. G2168 (give thanks) co-occurs with M72 (Lord/reign, G2962G/G0936) and M23 (Almighty/power, G3841/G1411): thanksgiving here is triggered specifically by God's assumption of kingly power and reign — the characteristic functions as the fitting liturgical response to a demonstrated act of sovereign power, tying gratitude directly to God's kingship.

First pass over this verse. H8426 (thanksgiving) co-occurs with M08/M16/M22 (praise, H1984B) and M22 (song H7892A, magnify H1431): thanksgiving here functions as the accompanying mode by which praise and magnification of God's name are carried out — the characteristic is instrumental, the means through which the larger act of exalting God's name is enacted.

In Ps.138.2, thanksgiving (H3034) is directed at the divine name and stands alongside steadfast love (M07/M50, H2617A), faithfulness (M13, H0571G), and exaltation (M22, H1431) -- thanksgiving here is the responsive verbal act that answers and publicly announces those other divine attributes; it is the vehicle by which love/faithfulness/exaltation become spoken acknowledgment.

In 2Chr.30.22, thanksgiving (H3034) co-occurs with skill/insight (M15, H7922), goodness (M05/M18, H2896A), and encouragement (M47, H3820A) -- thanksgiving is the culminating liturgical act performed by those already characterised by skilled, good service, showing thanksgiving as the fitting outward expression of an already-formed disposition.

In Dan.9.20, confession (H3034, penitential sense) is paired tightly with prayer/plea (M42, H6419/H8467) and sin (M56, H2403B) -- here thanksgiving's confessional branch functions not as praise but as the verbal admission accompanying supplication, distinguishing this occurrence from the praise-cluster co-occurrences seen elsewhere in the batch.

In 1Chr.16.4, thanksgiving (H3034) is grouped with invocation (M81, H2142) and praise (M08/M16/M22, H1984B) as the threefold liturgical service assigned to the Levites -- thanksgiving occupies the middle term between remembering/invoking God and praising him, marking it as the responsive acknowledgment phase of worship.

In 1Chr.23.30, thanksgiving pairs with praise (M08/M16/M22, H1984B) in a fixed daily (morning/evening) liturgical routine -- thanksgiving here is scheduled, habitual acknowledgment rather than a one-time response, distinguishing this occurrence's temporal-repetition framing from the other verses.

In 1Chr.25.3, thanksgiving co-occurs with prophesying (M43, H5012) and praise (M08/M16/M22, H1984B) -- thanksgiving is bound here to musical prophecy, showing the characteristic operating within an inspired/prophetic musical office rather than simple spoken response.

In 1Chr.29.13, thanksgiving and praise (M08/M16/M22, H1984B) are paired as the direct, corporate first-person response to God's glorious name -- thanksgiving here is the immediate communal reflex rather than an institutional office, contrasting with the priestly-office framing of 1Chr.16.4/23.30.

In 2Chr.5.13, thanksgiving (H3034) is bound with praise, singing (M22, H7891), and steadfast love/goodness (M07/M50/M05/M18) at the climactic moment the cloud fills the house -- thanksgiving here functions as the trigger-response that precedes and accompanies the manifestation of divine presence, a distinct causal-adjacency role not seen in the other verses.

In 2Chr.7.6, thanksgiving (H3034) is set alongside priestly service (M36, H3548), ministry (M23/M72, H3027I), and steadfast love (M07/M50) as an institution established 'by David' -- thanksgiving here is historically anchored to a founding royal ordinance, a durational/institutional framing distinct from the spontaneous congregational thanks of 1Chr.29.13.

In 2Chr.20.21, thanksgiving (H3034) co-occurs with counsel (M63, H3289), singing (M22), holiness (M61, H6944G), and steadfast love (M07/M50) in a martial-liturgical setting -- thanksgiving here precedes and accompanies the army's advance, functioning as a vocalised expression of trust that goes before military action rather than in a temple setting.
In Ps.138.2 the psalmist (first person) initiates the thanksgiving-operation directed toward 'your name' (the Lord), a first-person-to-divine-second-person direction.
In 2Chr.30.22 the Levites (party) initiate the thanksgiving-operation directed toward the Lord, God of their fathers, performed alongside peace-offering sacrifice.
In Dan.9.20 Daniel (first person, 'I') initiates the confessing-operation directed toward the Lord his God, alongside speaking and praying.
In 1Chr.16.4 the Levites, appointed by David (implied party), initiate the thanksgiving-operation directed toward the Lord, God of Israel, before the ark.
In 1Chr.23.30 the Levites (implied by verse context) initiate the standing thanksgiving-operation directed toward the Lord, performed daily morning and evening.
In 1Chr.25.3 the sons of Jeduthun (party) initiate the thanksgiving-operation directed toward the Lord, performed with the lyre under prophetic inspiration.
In 1Chr.29.13 'we' (the assembly, first person plural) initiate the thanksgiving-operation directed toward 'you, our God'.
In 2Chr.5.13 the trumpeters and singers (party) initiate the thanksgiving-operation directed toward the Lord, in unison with musical instruments.

In 2Chr.7.6 King David (party) is the initiating agent who made the instruments 'for giving thanks to the Lord'; the operation is directed toward the Lord and executed by the Levites/priests he established.
In 2Chr.20.21 those appointed to sing (party, appointed by Jehoshaphat) initiate the thanksgiving-operation ('Give thanks') directed toward the Lord, going before the army.

The verse's operation-tagged word is H7725I (turn away, role-T3), initiated by God's anger (subject) turning away from the speaker (object/beneficiary). H3034 itself (thanks) is not tagged role-T3 in this verse's role list (it carries only M49), so no D7.7.1 relation is recorded for H3034 as an operation-word; it is the responsive speech-act, not the operation.

Building on the prior finding (thanksgiving as capstone response to anger-turned-comfort): from thanksgiving's own vantage, this occurrence shows the characteristic functioning prospectively as well -- 'you will say... I will give thanks' -- meaning the thanksgiving is anticipated and rehearsed as the fitting future speech-act that will properly name and close the sequence of divine anger (M02) and comfort (M11/M45), underscoring that thanksgiving is the verbal seal that completes, not merely accompanies, the relational reversal.

Building on the prior finding (thanksgiving names/ratifies glory, goodness, and steadfast love just witnessed): from thanksgiving's own vantage, the act is performed corporately and physically embodied (bowing faces to the ground) alongside worship (H7812), showing that here thanksgiving is not a solitary verbal act but a communal liturgical response that binds the whole assembly's acknowledgment of God's glory (M22) and covenant love (M07/M50) into a single ritual moment.

Building on the prior finding (thanksgiving grounded in the recipients' faith being proclaimed): from thanksgiving's own vantage, this shows the characteristic functioning here as an apostolic relational bridge -- Paul's thanks moves through Christ toward God and is triggered by observing another party's M13 (faith) at work in the world, illustrating thanksgiving's role as the verbal link connecting observed virtue in others to praise of God as its ultimate source.

Building on the prior finding (thanksgiving as the verbal pivot resolving the M78/M54/M15/M47/M56 conflict): from thanksgiving's own vantage, its exclamatory, non-finite grammatical form here (a bare nominal cry rather than a declared act) shows the characteristic bursting forth spontaneously at the resolution point, functioning less as a considered statement and more as an immediate relational release triggered by deliverance from the enslaving characteristics named in the verse.

Building on the prior finding (thanksgiving grounded in grace given in Christ Jesus): from thanksgiving's own vantage, the characteristic here operates as continual/habitual ('always') rather than a single act, showing thanksgiving functioning as a settled ongoing posture toward M50 (grace) rather than a one-time response.

Building on the prior finding (thanksgiving and prayer, G4336, as companion but distinct acts): from thanksgiving's own vantage, it is positioned temporally as the frame within which prayer occurs ('we thank... when we pray'), showing thanksgiving functions as the constant disposition of communication with God that specific petitionary prayer sits inside, rather than the two being interchangeable synonyms.

Building on the prior finding (thankfulness accompanying Christ's peace, M33, ruling the heart, M47): from thankfulness's own vantage, being commanded as the concluding imperative of the verse shows it functioning as the capstone disposition that should characterize the 'one body' called to peace -- thankfulness here is the fitting communal response that completes and stabilizes the peace-governed, united heart just described.

No other M-code characteristic co-occurs alongside thanksgiving (G2168) in 1Thess.5.18's role list (M18 'will' is present but that is a different M-code from a distinct characteristic, not overlapping here in a relational way the role list marks); recorded as the sole M-code characteristic directly relevant to thanksgiving's own field of view in this verse's role tags.

Building on the prior finding (praise as response to awe/holiness): from praise's own vantage point, the verb itself supplies the missing verbal enactment the awesome/holy name calls for — M01 and M13/M61 name the divine attributes that make the name praiseworthy, while H3034 supplies the community's required liturgical action, closing the loop between attribute and response.

H3034 ('let them praise') is the role-T3-tagged operation in this verse; it is initiated by the implied worshipping community ('them') and directed toward God, whose great, awesome, and holy name/person is the object of the praise-act.

Building on the prior finding (confession situates thanksgiving within intercessory prayer grounded in covenant love): from confession's own vantage point, H3034 is the specific speech-act by which Daniel acknowledges both God's covenant-faithfulness (M44, M07/M50) and, implicitly, the people's failure to keep commandments (M54) — confession functions as the pivot connecting praise of God's character to the acknowledgment of human breach that the following verses will detail.

H3034 here is tagged M49 not role-T3; the role-T3 operation word in this verse is 'saying' (H0559), spoken by Daniel, but that word attaches to the prayer discourse generally rather than constituting an H3034-specific operation-party relation.

Building on the prior finding (thanksgiving as the fitting response to God's assumption of reign/power): from thanksgiving's own vantage point, G2168 is voiced corporately ('we') by the twenty-four elders, showing the characteristic functioning here as the collective, first-person liturgical acknowledgment specifically of a completed act of sovereign power (M72, M23), not merely a general attribute.

G2168 ('give thanks') is tagged M49 not role-T3; the role-T3 operation present is 'taken' (G2983, 'you have taken your great power'), initiated by God and directed toward assuming sovereign reign — the thanksgiving act of the elders responds to, rather than performs, this operation.

Building on the prior finding (thanksgiving as the instrumental means by which praise/magnification is enacted): from thanksgiving's own vantage point, H8426 here functions grammatically as the accompanying-manner term (with a preposition) rather than the main verb, showing thanksgiving cast as the mode/vehicle carrying the psalmist's praise (M08/M16/M22) and magnifying (M22) of God's name, subordinate to those acts rather than co-equal with them.

H8426 in this verse is not tagged role-T3 (only M49); the role-T3 operation is H1984B (praise), initiated by the psalmist ('I') and directed toward God's name, with thanksgiving serving as its accompanying manner rather than a separate operation.

Building on the prior finding that thanksgiving answers love/faithfulness/exaltation: from thanksgiving's own vantage, it is the SOLE verbal-response mechanism in the verse that converts three separate divine attributes (steadfast love M07/M50, faithfulness M13, exaltation M22) into one unified act of acknowledgment -- without H3034 these attributes would remain unspoken states; thanksgiving supplies the only verb of address directed at the divine name itself.

Building on the prior finding that thanksgiving culminates good/skilled service here: from thanksgiving's vantage, it is paired with peace offerings (M33) as the verbal counterpart to the physical sacrificial act -- the two together (sacrifice + thanks) form a complete offering-response unit, with thanksgiving supplying the spoken half no other M-code in this verse provides.

Building on the prior finding that confession here functions penitentially alongside prayer and sin: from confession's own vantage, it is the operative link binding sin (M56) to prayer/plea (M42) -- confession names what prayer is FOR, converting M42's general 'seeking' into a specific penitential seeking, since without confession the plea would lack its stated object (the sin admitted).

Building on the prior finding of thanksgiving as the middle term between invocation and praise: from thanksgiving's own vantage, it is the pivot that requires both a prior remembering (invocation, M81) and gives rise to an ensuing acclamation (praise, M08/M16/M22) -- structurally it cannot stand alone in this triad, marking it as transitional rather than terminal.

Building on the prior finding of thanksgiving's daily-routine pairing with praise: from thanksgiving's vantage, it supplies the content-specific half (acknowledging particular divine acts/attributes) while praise (M08/M16/M22) supplies the general acclamatory half -- together they form a complete twice-daily liturgical unit, with thanksgiving anchoring the 'what for' that praise alone leaves unspecified.

Building on the prior finding that thanksgiving is bound to prophesying here: from thanksgiving's own vantage, it supplies the RECOGNIZABLE liturgical content (words of thanks) that gives the prophetic musical act (M43) its verbal shape -- without thanksgiving's specific content, the prophesying-with-lyre would be an undefined musical utterance rather than a defined act of praise.

Building on the prior finding that thanksgiving/praise are the direct communal reflex here: from thanksgiving's vantage, it is grammatically and semantically the FIRST verb of the pair ('we thank...and praise'), establishing the object (God's glorious name) that the following praise-verb (M08/M16/M22) then elaborates -- thanksgiving names the addressee-focused act, praise extends it descriptively.

Building on the prior finding of thanksgiving as trigger-response preceding the cloud's appearance: from thanksgiving's own vantage, it functions with praise/singing (M22) and steadfast love/goodness (M07/M50/M05/M18) as one of three co-terms making up 'unison' -- but is distinctively the term that supplies the CONTENT clause quoted ('he is good, his steadfast love endures forever'), meaning thanksgiving here carries the propositional content the other M-codes only characterise emotionally.

Building on the prior finding that thanksgiving is anchored to David's founding ordinance alongside priestly service and ministry: from thanksgiving's own vantage, it is the specific ACT that priestly service (M36) and ministry (M23/M72) were instituted to perform -- the other M-codes describe the office/role, thanksgiving names the office's actual content and purpose.

Building on the prior finding of thanksgiving preceding the army's advance: from thanksgiving's own vantage, it is the final, climactic verb in a chain that begins with counsel (M63) and singing (M22) -- thanksgiving supplies the actual spoken content ('his steadfast love endures forever') that the counsel decided should be voiced and the singing was to carry, making it the terminus of the other M-codes' preparatory action.

H3034 ('give thanks,' HVhu1cs) is the operation-tagged verb of thanksgiving-relevance in this verse, though role-T3 is not itself marked on H3034 here; the clear role-T3 operation is H7812 'bow down' -- initiated by the psalmist (first person) and directed toward God's holy temple, establishing the posture that the following thanksgiving-act (H3034) then verbally performs toward God's name.

Role-T3 operation words present are 'ate' (H0398) and 'sacrificing' (H2076), initiated by the Levites/people party toward the Lord (offerings) -- H3034 thanksgiving itself is tagged M49 not T3 here, but it accompanies these operations as their concurrent verbal expression, directed at 'the Lord, the God of their fathers.'

Role-T3 operation is 'speaking' (H1696G, M42/T3), initiated by Daniel (first person 'I') and directed toward the Lord his God, with confessing (H3034) naming the specific content of that directed speech-operation.

Role-T3 operation 'appointed' (H5414H) is initiated by an unnamed royal/administrative subject (David, per context) directed toward the Levites, assigning them the subsequent acts of invoking, thanking (H3034), and praising the Lord -- thanksgiving is the assigned task-object of the appointing operation.

Role-T3 operation 'stand' (H5975G) is initiated by the Levites and is directed toward the Lord as its recipient/object of the accompanying acts of thanking (H3034) and praising -- standing is the physical operation that frames the verbal acts.

No independent role-T3 operation word co-occurs with H3034 as a separate tagged item in this verse's role list beyond the thanksgiving/praise verbs themselves (H1984B tagged T3); praise here is initiated by Jeduthun's sons under his direction, toward the Lord.

Role-T3 operation is 'praise' (H1984B), initiated by the corporate 'we' and directed toward God's glorious name, running in parallel with thanksgiving (H3034) as the co-ordinate first verb of the same directed pair.

Role-T3 operations 'trumpeters' (making sound, H2690) and 'praise' (H1984B) are initiated by the trumpeters/singers party and directed toward the Lord, with thanksgiving (H3034) co-occurring as the accompanying verbal content of the same directed act, immediately followed by the cloud filling the house.

Role-T3 operations 'stood' (H5975G) and 'sounded trumpets' (H2690) are initiated by the priests/Levites party and directed toward the Lord in the temple setting, with thanksgiving (H3034, tied to David's ordinance) naming the purpose these standing/sounding operations serve.

Role-T3 operations 'appointed' (H5975H) and 'went' (H3318G) are initiated by the unnamed leader (Jehoshaphat, per context) directed toward the singers/people, who then march before the army; the imperative thanksgiving (H3034) is the content the appointed singers are commanded to voice toward the Lord.
No other M-code characteristic co-occurs in this verse; the surrounding priestly-service and offering terms (H5656H, H5930A) are not tagged with M-codes carrying their own cluster.

No role-T3 operation tag is attached to H3034 itself in this verse; the operation tags present (H5975H 'appointed', H5930A 'burnt offerings') belong to other words, so D7.7.1 does not apply to H3034 here.

Other M-codes present (M22 praise, M05/M18 good, M07/M50 steadfast love, M84 shout) surround H3034 in a worship scene, but H3034 functions as the lead thanksgiving verb introducing the antiphonal song rather than being conceptually dependent on any one of them; it initiates the liturgical sequence that M22/M84 continue.

H3034 itself is not tagged role-T3 in this verse (the T3 operation tags belong to H6030C 'sang responsively', H1984B 'praising', H3245 'foundation-laid'); those operations are directed by the people/singers toward the Lord as party, but D7.7.1 records this under the operation-word's own strong, not H3034.

Other M-codes present (M24/M72 chiefs, M08/M16/M22 praise, M54 commandment) surround H3034 within a description of Levitical duty rotation; H3034 names one of the two paired liturgical duties (praise and thanks) assigned by commandment, but does not derive its meaning from the office-terms themselves.

M44 (congregation) and M23 (mighty/numerous) are present alongside H3034 in this verse; H3034 names the act performed within the assembly (M44) described as great/mighty (M23), the relationship being locative/circumstantial rather than definitional overlap.

M08/M16/M22 (praise) and M05/M18 (good) and M07/M50 (steadfast love) all appear in this compact hymnic verse; H3034 stands as the responsive human act evoked BY God's goodness and steadfast love, forming the standard call-and-response pattern of Hebrew hymnody rather than a direct semantic merger with those other characteristics.

M08/M16/M22 (praise) co-occurs alongside H3034 as its parallel synonym in this verse's poetic structure ('give thanks... praise'); H3034 supplies the vocal/mouth-oriented aspect (paired with H6310G 'mouth') while praise (M22) supplies the public exaltation aspect -- complementary rather than overlapping.

M08/M16/M22 (praise), M47 (heart), M16 (company/council) appear together; H3034 anchors the whole-hearted (M47) vow of thanksgiving performed within the gathered upright company (M16), each M-code contributing a distinct dimension (manner, location, disposition) to the single act H3034 names.

M08/M16/M22 (praise) and M68 (hope) and M13 (faithfulness) co-occur; H3034 is negated in parallel with praise (M22), both impossible for the dead, while hope (M68) and faithfulness (M13) belong to a distinct clause about the living seeking God -- H3034 relates to praise as paired negated impossibility, not to hope/faithfulness directly.

M08/M16/M22 (boasted, same root H1984H) co-occurs; H3034 stands as the parallel synonym continuing the same idea of glorying in God's name, forming a synonymous doublet rather than a distinct relational link.

M03/M16/M71 (glorifies), M15 (orders/sets), M76 (way), M79 (salvation) are present alongside H8426 in this verse; the offering of thanksgiving (H8426) is what results in glorifying God (M03/M16/M71), while ordering one's way (M15/M76) is a separate condition for receiving salvation (M79) -- H8426 causally links to the glorify-verb but not to the way/salvation terms directly.

H8426 itself is not tagged role-T3 (it is a noun, object of the operation 'offers/sacrifices' H2076 which is role-T3); that operation is directed by 'the one who offers' toward God as recipient, with H8426 as the offered content -- recorded under the operation word's own strong, not H8426.
In Ps.86.12 no other M-code characteristic co-occurs with thanksgiving (H3034); the verse's other tagged content is grammatical/role scaffolding, not another M-code member.

In Ezra.10.1, confession (H3034) co-occurs with M42 (prayer, H6419) and M03 (weeping, H1058, twice), M44 (assembly), M02/M50 (prostration before God's house). Confession here functions as the vocal centerpiece of a broader penitential scene: prayer initiates address to God, weeping expresses grief, and confession names the specific content (sin) being brought before God -- confession supplies the articulate, content-bearing act that the other M-codes (prayer, weeping) surround with posture and emotion.
